neighbours.label: Opening quote mark right after the narration shows someone handing or offering something to another person: the moment an offering line ('Here, ...') is about to be spoken. The - pole is the other side: requests to the speaker ('Give me', 'Bring on').
fire: Marta slid the bowl of stew across the table to him. "It's still warm, so mind your tongue."
The nurse pressed a cup of water into his hands. "Small sips, there's no hurry."
Grandpa held the umbrella out to the girl. "Keep it, the rain won't stop tonight."
Tom passed his jacket over to his sister. "Put this on, you're shivering."
The waiter set a basket of bread in front of them. "On the house, folks."
She tucked a folded banknote into the boy's pocket. "For the bus, and a little extra."
The teacher handed the girl a fresh pencil. "Try again, slowly this time."
He poured a mug of tea and pushed it toward his guest. "Drink up, it will settle your nerves."
quiet: Marta slammed the ledger shut and glared at him. "You were supposed to be here at noon."
The nurse checked the chart at the foot of the bed. "When did the fever start?"
Grandpa squinted at the clouds over the barn. "I've never seen a sky that colour."
Tom threw his jacket on the floor and turned on his sister. "Give me back my phone right now."
The waiter glanced at his watch and sighed. "The kitchen closed ten minutes ago."
She crossed her arms and stared at the boy. "Tell me where you were last night."
The teacher tapped the blackboard with her ruler. "Who can give me the answer?"
He leaned back and laughed at his guest. "I can't believe you fell for that."

notes: Card: peaks on sentence starts before kindly directives (Get up, Here, Buy yourself); output promotes Enjoy/yourself and suppresses me/give/please. Probe: the opening quote after 'pushed the plate toward her' scored 0.72 whatever was said next, and 0.03 after a frown, so the trigger is the giving gesture before the quote, not the quoted words.
